title: Value per unit weight of items
summary: Value per unit weight equals item value divided by weight; taking weight w of an item adds w times its value per unit weight to the knapsack.
context: Because fractional knapsack allows splitting items, comparing value per unit weight determines priority better than comparing whole-item values alone.
description: On the left, the table lists the five items by original ID with fruit icons transcribed as names. Its fourth column, "Value per unit weight val[i - 1] / wgt[i - 1]", prints 5, 6, 5, 5.25, and 4.8 directly in the figure rather than adding an external column. On the right, weight taken w multiplied by value per unit weight gives "Value added to the knapsack".

frames.title: Value per unit weight of items
frames.explanation: For example, the apple's value per unit weight is 50 ÷ 10 = 5. On the right, Weight taken from the current item w × Value per unit weight val[i - 1] / wgt[i - 1] = Value added to the knapsack, holding whether an item is taken whole or in part. Across the table, banana has the highest unit value, followed by pineapple.
